rows.jp: そうして俺たちは、桐原のお屋敷に行った。
rows.en: So we went to the Kirihara estate.

ghs.en: And then we went to the Kirihara Mansion.

rows.jp: 「とりあえず、これだけ！」
rows.en: “For now, just this much!”

ghs.en: Touko: "For now, it's just these!"

rows.jp: これだけ。
rows.en: Just this much.

ghs.en: Just these,

rows.jp: きゃつはそう言った。
rows.en: So said the fiend.

ghs.en: the gal went and said.
ghs.assessment: きゃつ is a contemptuous or mock-archaic 'that knave/fellow.' 'The gal' identifies sex but loses the narrator's pointedly derisive register.

rows.jp: リヤカーにして三台分ほどあった。
rows.en: Enough to fill about three handcarts.

ghs.en: There were about three bike trailer loads,
ghs.assessment: A リヤカー is a two-wheeled handcart. 'Bike trailer' specifies a bicycle-towed vehicle and changes the object used for the three-load estimate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There were about three handcart-loads in all.'

highlights.text: There were about three bike trailer loads,

rows.jp: そこで桐原家の大きなキャンピングカーを使うことにした。
rows.en: We decided to use the Kirihara family’s enormous RV.

ghs.en: so we went and used the Kiriharas' huge RV.

rows.jp: これでも運転はできる。
rows.en: Even I could drive.

ghs.en: But I can drive even this,

rows.jp: 走り屋マンガで学んだからだ。
rows.en: I’d learned from street-racing manga.

ghs.en: because I've studied racing mangas.

rows.jp: ……見るとやるとでは大違いだった。
rows.en: ...It turned out watching and doing were two very different things.

ghs.en: ...between the saying and the doing there is a vast difference in difficulty.

rows.jp: いろいろあったが、とりあえず冬子はトラウマになった。
rows.en: Things happened. Suffice it to say, Touko was traumatized.

ghs.en: Several things have happened, the main of which is that Touko has become traumatized.
ghs.assessment: The source says only that various things happened and that, in any case, Tōko was traumatized. 'The main of which' invents a ranking and makes the trauma one event in a relative-clause list.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A lot happened, but in any case Tōko was traumatized.'

highlights.text: Several things have happened, the main of which is that Touko has become traumatized.

rows.jp: 二度と俺の車には乗らないとまで言った。
rows.en: She even swore she’d never ride in my car again.

ghs.en: To the point where she said she would never ride a vehicle with me driving again.
ghs.assessment: 俺の車 is the narrator's car. 'A vehicle with me driving' generalizes her vow to every vehicle he might drive.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She even said she would never ride in my car again.'

highlights.text: To the point where she said she would never ride a vehicle with me driving again.

rows.jp: 同感である。
rows.en: I couldn’t blame her.

ghs.en: I am of the same opinion.

rows.jp: いやー、シートベルトしていて本当に良かった。
rows.en: Boy, was I glad we’d worn our seat belts.

ghs.en: Welll, it was a good thing we had seatbelts.

rows.jp: とにかく『黒須家近所までは車を使えた』ので、あとはそこから移動すればよかった。
rows.en: At least we’d managed to drive as far as my neighborhood. From there, all we had to do was move everything.

ghs.en: Anyway, we managed to walk away from the "Let's Use a Vehicle Up to the Neighborhood of the Kurosu Residence" plan, which was good.
ghs.assessment: The source says they were able to use the vehicle as far as the neighborhood of the Kurosu residence and only had to move the load from there. 'Walk away from the plan' says that they abandoned the plan and omits the successful transport stage.
ghs.remedy: Say that the car got them as far as the Kurosu neighborhood, leaving only the move from there.

highlights.text: Anyway, we managed to walk away from the "Let's Use a Vehicle Up to the Neighborhood of the Kurosu Residence" plan, which was good.

rows.jp: とはいえ距離にして数百メートルはあってだな。
rows.en: Granted, “from there” was still several hundred meters.

ghs.en: Nonetheless, there were still several hundred meters of distance.

rows.jp: 俺と冬子はリヤカーを探した。
rows.en: Touko and I went looking for a handcart.

ghs.en: Me and Touko searched for a bike trailer.
ghs.assessment: 'Me and Touko' uses the object pronoun as the subject of the sentence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko and I searched for a handcart.'

highlights.text: Me and Touko searched for a bike trailer.

rows.jp: 冬子などはご令嬢であるためかリヤカーというものをフロントにカゴのついたママチャリだと勘違いしていたので、貧乏人代表として怒りの乳揉みをしてやった。
rows.en: Apparently, in sheltered-heiress world, a handcart was a bicycle with a basket on the front. As the official representative of the poor, I lodged a complaint by squeezing a tit.

ghs.en: Perhaps because Touko is so much of an young milady from a rich family, when she mistakenly claimed that a granny bike was a 'trailer' because it had a basket on the front, as a representative of the poor people I massaged her breasts in anger.
ghs.assessment: The English begins with the ungrammatical article sequence 'an young,' calls the mamachari a 'granny bike,' and weakens the narrator's aggressive 胸揉み from groping or kneading her breasts to a neutral massage.
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical sentence that identifies the basket-equipped mamachari and preserves the deliberately improper breast-groping action.

highlights.text: Perhaps because Touko is so much of an young milady from a rich family, when she mistakenly claimed that a granny bike was a 'trailer' because it had a basket on the front, as a representative of the poor people I massaged her breasts in anger.

rows.jp: 殴られた。いいことだ。
rows.en: She punched me. Excellent.

ghs.en: I was punched. That is good.

rows.jp: で、俺が探し出したリヤカーで三往復。
rows.en: Then we made three round trips with the handcart I’d found.

ghs.en: Then, with a trailer we found, I made three round trips.
ghs.assessment: The source says that the narrator found the handcart. 'We found' changes the finder to the pair.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Then I made three round trips with the handcart I found.'

highlights.text: Then, with a trailer we found, I made three round trips.

rows.jp: 疲労困憊(こんぱい)。
rows.en: I was dead on my feet.

ghs.en: Fatigue at extreme levels.
ghs.assessment: 疲労困憊 is the complete state of being utterly exhausted. 'Fatigue at extreme levels' is an abstract degree fragment rather than an idiomatic account of the narrator's condition.

rows.jp: そんな俺をさらに叩きのめしたのは冬子の言葉だった。
rows.en: Then Touko finished me off with one sentence.

ghs.en: And I was furthermore struck down by Touko's words.

rows.jp: 部屋に案内した第一声。
rows.en: The first thing she said when I showed her the room:

ghs.en: The first thing that she said once I led her to her room was,

rows.jp: 「……なに、この物置？」
rows.en: “...What is this, a storage closet?”

ghs.en: Touko: "...what's even this storeroom?"
ghs.assessment: 'What's even this storeroom?' is not grammatical English question order and does not naturally convey the dismissive なに、この construction.

rows.jp: そこで力尽きて、崩れ落ちた。
rows.en: That was it. I crumpled to the floor.

ghs.en: And there, all my strength used up, I collapsed.
